name: Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes
summary: Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes tracks a roster of more than 300 characters, each advancing through its own level, star rank, gear tier and ability track, fed by battles, quests and a wide currency economy. Nearly every hub feature stays locked behind a stated player level or character measure, visible in its eventual position from the very first screen. An Episode Track pays free and paid reward lanes from quest points, while crystal-priced loot packs and a free daily draw both resolve to characters and shards from a stated pool. Three separate energy pools gate light side, cantina and fleet battles, refilling on their own schedules or for a price.
teaser: In the opening hours, level-up bonuses gave players more energy than they could spend — one reading showed 158 held against a stated maximum of 68.

observations.name: Tracking permission request
observations.observed: The first thing the app shows on first open is the system request asking whether it may track the user across other apps and websites, before any game content or account screen appears.

observations.name: Import or new player
observations.observed: The app asks whether the user has an account already, offering Import Account or New Player. Import Account offers a single sign-in method, EA Connect, opening the EA Connect website inside the app rather than in an external browser, and states that an existing account not yet linked should be linked from the old device first. New Player starts a loading screen with scenes and characters from the films. No account creation, email or password is required to start as a new player, and import remains available later from settings.

observations.name: Guided first battle
observations.observed: A new player is placed straight into a battle with two characters an alien guide announces are now in the roster. The guide instructs each move in turn, and other controls do not respond while the guide leads. On victory the guide announces the first battle rewards, and a rewards screen states that completing battles earns player XP and collects crystals, shards, credits and other items.

tags.name: Experience Points
tags.confidence:
directly observed
**Role:** engagement
Player XP and character XP are granted for battles, quest claims and droid training inside sessions and move the level states (O3, O18, O22, O23).
**Rationale:** The rewards screen states that battles earn player XP, a daily quest lists an XP reward, and claiming journey quests grants XP (O3, O18, O25) (tier: directly observed). The accumulated value produces player level-ups, with a displayed 6 of 10 at level 2 (O22) (tier: directly observed). Character training shows a separate XP bar such as 0 of 25, filled by assigning training droids of different grades (O23) (tier: directly observed). The XP is not spent in any exchange (tier: directly observed).
**Variants present:** Account XP (O22). Character XP (O23). Unified XP, with battles, daily quests and journey quests all granting player XP (O3, O18, O25). Variable-grant XP, with higher-grade training droids giving more character XP (O23).
**Variants not established:** Threshold-reset XP against rollover XP, because the display across a level-up was not described. Capped XP, seasonal XP and expiring XP.
**Alternative considered:** Spendable Credits and Tokens was considered for training droids, which are spent; the droids are consumed items that grant XP, and the XP itself is not exchanged, so the droids are described in plain language (O38). The "0 out of 15" figure on the first hub view is read as XP only by the narrator (O4) and is not relied on.

observations.name: Hub shown, controls locked
observations.observed: After the first battle the hub loads in full, showing a player level indicator, a Collection button, padlocked Journey Guide, Allies and Inbox buttons, two currencies, and characters standing at tables for battles, the arena, the store, shipments, campaigns, mod battles and challenges. A Coliseum timer and a character event countdown are visible. Tapping settings, Collection or the currencies does nothing at this point; only Quests responds.

tags.name: Progression Gate
tags.confidence:
directly observed
**Role:** engagement
The gates stage which tables, modes and tiers the player can use as levels, star ranks and gear tiers advance through play (O22, O30, O31, O32).
**Rationale:** Galaxy of Heroes withholds most hub features until a stated player level, with the requirement shown when the locked table is tapped (O30) (tier: directly observed). Other parts are gated on measures the product also advances: number of dark side characters, a character's level, a character's star rank, a gear tier, completion of named battles and completion of a normal stage (O31, O32) (tier: directly observed). Each withheld part is distinct from the measure it reads (tier: directly observed). Requirements that include joining a guild, such as the Gifts tab and guild raids, carry a condition the product does not advance through a progression measure; that condition is recorded in plain language, and only the level and gear requirements in those cases fall under this tag (O31) (tier: directly observed). The Episode Pass requirement on some quest rewards is a purchase requirement and is excluded (O33) (tier: directly observed). The hard mode five-per-day limit is a rate limiter and is excluded (O16) (tier: directly observed). The next campaign node is the next unit of the campaign and is excluded (O32) (tier: directly observed).
**Variants present:** Level gate (O30). Composite gate, for dark side battles, mod battles, ships and guild raids (O31). Stage gate, for hard mode, mod challenges and the Journey Guide route through Rebels 5 (O10, O31, O32). Count gate, for collecting one datacron and holding three dark side characters (O31). Opaque gate, for tables represented only by a requirement message (O30). Undescribed gate, for the Scavenger, where the narrator asks what relic amplifiers are (O31). Staggered gates (O30). Announced unlock gate, through level-up messages and guide introductions (O22). Silent unlock gate, for Allies (O30). Bypassable gate, for the Journey Guide's "player level 27 or complete Rebels 5" (O31).
**Variants not established:** Browsable gate, because whether locked features can be explored before unlocking was not shown. Previewed gate. Reinstating gate. Per-position gate.
**Alternative considered:** Leveling and Milestone classify the measure and the crossing and are tagged separately. Seasonal Progression Pass was considered for the pass-only quest rewards, which the purchase exclusion removes from this tag. Energy was considered for the hard mode daily limit, which governs how often rather than whether.

observations.name: First quest, Go button
observations.observed: Opening Quests shows Daily Quests locked, Journey Quests open, and Achievements and Guild Activities tabs locked. The guide states that quests always show what to do next and that the Go button always leads to where the current quest is completed. Tapping Go moves the player directly to the Light Side battles map.

observations.name: Second guided battle
observations.observed: The first Light Side node shows a description, possible enemies, first-time rewards and an energy cost. The squad screen states that no other light side characters are available yet. In battle the guide teaches tap-and-hold for ability details, a status effect icon, and an enemy's Taunt, and a 1x, 2x and 4x speed control appears. The battle ends in a three-star victory and a player level-up, which states that max energy increased and 20 bonus energy was earned.

observations.name: Asset downloads deferred
observations.observed: No download is shown before the first battle. After the second battle a download runs in the background, and later a pop-up states that further assets will download over the wireless network. Downloading continues while the player uses the store and draws a data card.

observations.name: Birth month and name
observations.observed: After the second battle and an era announcement, a pop-up asks for birth month and year with a checkbox accepting the EA User Agreement and privacy policy, followed by a screen asking the player to choose a name, stating it will be visible to other players and should not include personal information. These steps come after two battles rather than at first launch, and the first paid offer appears immediately after the name is chosen.

observations.name: Guided character upgrades
observations.observed: Early journey quests lead into guided upgrade actions: training a character with a training droid, activating a character for credits, promoting a character once enough shards are held, and equipping gear, with the guide explaining that legacy characters use gear while era units do not. On a squad screen the guide explains the leader slot and the benefit indicator, and later battles introduce the speed bar and turn order tracker. Only the element the guide names is tappable during these first steps.

observations.name: Forced hard mode battle
observations.observed: After the six normal battles of the first stage, at player level 5, the guide states that hard mode is now unlocked and calls it the best place to find character shards. The player cannot skip this battle, change characters or upgrade anyone before it. After the victory, the guide states that normal and hard mode can now be chosen when a stage is complete, and that each hard mode battle can be completed five times a day to earn its rewards.

tags.name: Milestone
tags.confidence:
directly observed
**Role:** engagement
Level-up screens mark what has just opened and grant bonus energy, and the hard mode notice marks the end of a stage, both within ongoing play (O10, O22).
**Rationale:** A player level-up produces a separate screen that states "You have unlocked shipments" or a similar unlock and awards 20 bonus energy, beyond the change in the level number (O22) (tier: directly observed). Completing all normal battles in the first stage produces the guide's hard mode unlock message (O10) (tier: directly observed). Both events are tied to position in a broader progression (tier: directly observed).
**Variants present:** Unlocking milestone (O10, O22). Rewarded milestone, with bonus energy on each level-up (O22). Stage milestone, for stage completion opening hard mode (O10).
**Variants not established:** Recorded milestone, because no history of reached levels was seen. Hidden milestone.
**Alternative considered:** Achievement was considered, and the level-up screens create no separately preserved attained record, while the Achievements tab is tagged on its own (O27). Progression Gate classifies the standing requirement in front of each feature and also applies, as that entry allows.

observations.name: Free starter items
observations.observed: Returning to the cantina, the guide offers a free character in the cantina store, unlocking a character for free through a data card. The store then shows two further free items, a training droids gift pack and a sim tickets gift pack, each labelled as good for new players.

tags.name: Soft Currency
tags.confidence:
directly observed
**Role:** engagement, social
Credits, cantina tokens and sim tickets are earned by playing and spent on upgrades, shipments and instant completions within sessions (O17, O35, O37), and ally points are earned only by fielding another player's unit (O36, O45).
**Rationale:** Credits are earned in battles and spent on training, activation, promotion, abilities and shipments (O35) (tier: directly observed). Ally points are earned by borrowing units and are described as spendable on Bronzium draws and weekly shipments (O36) (tier: directly observed). No ally point spend was recorded (tier: directly observed). Cantina battle tokens are earned per cantina battle and priced at 200 to 400 in the cantina store (O37) (tier: directly observed). No token spend was recorded (tier: directly observed). Sim tickets are earned from battles and gift packs and spent to complete battles instantly (O11, O17) (tier: directly observed). Crystals also have stated non-paid earning paths (O34) (tier: directly observed).
**Variants present:** Activity-earned soft currency (O35, O37). Quest-earned soft currency, through the daily prize box (O18). Login-grant soft currency, through login reward credits (O64). Social-earned soft currency, for ally points (O36). General-purpose soft currency, for credits (O35). Restricted soft currency, for cantina tokens and ally points (O36, O37). Dual-path soft currency, for crystals and credits (O34, O35). Multi-currency soft-currency system (O34 to O37).
**Variants not established:** Capped-earning, expiring and transferable soft currency.
**Alternative considered:** Boosters was considered for sim tickets and does not apply, because a ticket obtains a completed battle outside any battle instance rather than changing one. Energy does not apply to these balances, because each spend is a deliberate exchange.

observations.name: Auto battle and speed
observations.observed: An Auto control lets characters fight without the player choosing moves, continuing until stopped, and battle speed can be set to 1x, 2x or 4x.

observations.name: Three battle campaigns
observations.observed: The Campaigns table holds Light Side Battles, Dark Side Battles and Cantina Battles. observations.name: Energy pools per battle
observations.observed: Energy is described as the currency used to participate in light side and dark side battles, with separate pools for ship energy and cantina energy. The first Light Side node costs 6 energy and a cantina battle costs 8 cantina energy. Cantina energy refreshes by one point every 12 minutes, or 120 cantina energy can be bought for 100 crystals. Each level-up raises max energy and grants 20 bonus energy.

observations.name: Squad composition
observations.observed: The squad screen shows squad power, the leader ability and slots for adding or swapping characters. The character in the first slot is the leader and grants bonuses to the others, shown with a circle indicator for how much each ally benefits. A Squads tab lets the player create, save and organize multiple squads. A sixth slot is added at player level 18, reserved for a unit borrowed from another player.

observations.name: Player level and unlocks
observations.observed: Battles and quest claims grant player XP, and player level rises from 1 to 16 over the course of play. Each level-up screen states that max energy increased and awards 20 bonus energy, and also names what has just opened and what opens next, such as shipments unlocking, cantina battles unlocking in one level, or challenges unlocking with events and allies named further out.

tags.name: Leveling
tags.confidence:
directly observed
**Role:** engagement
Player level and the four character tracks are the states the player advances through battles and upgrade spending within sessions (O22, O23).
**Rationale:** The player level is a current discrete state that rises from 1 to 16 as XP accumulates (O22) (tier: directly observed). Each character holds separate ordered states: a character level raised with training droids, a star rank from one to seven raised by promotion, a gear tier raised when six slots are filled, and ability levels from one to eight (O23) (tier: directly observed). The Era of Andor view shows a total era level with a reward at the next level (O29) (tier: directly observed). The rule that moves era level was not shown (tier: directly observed).
**Variants present:** XP-driven leveling, for player level and character level (O22, O23). Criteria-based leveling, for gear tier and star rank (O23). Automatic leveling, for player level-ups (O22). Claimed leveling, for promotions and gear tier upgrades that need a tap once the conditions are met (O9, O23). Multi-track leveling (O23). directly observed
**Role:** engagement
The gates stage which tables, modes and tiers the player can use as levels, star ranks and gear tiers advance through play (O22, O30, O31, O32).
**Rationale:** Galaxy of Heroes withholds most hub features until a stated player level, with the requirement shown when the locked table is tapped (O30) (tier: directly observed). Other parts are gated on measures the product also advances: number of dark side characters, a character's level, a character's star rank, a gear tier, completion of named battles and completion of a normal stage (O31, O32) (tier: directly observed). Each withheld part is distinct from the measure it reads (tier: directly observed). Requirements that include joining a guild, such as the Gifts tab and guild raids, carry a condition the product does not advance through a progression measure; that condition is recorded in plain language, and only the level and gear requirements in those cases fall under this tag (O31) (tier: directly observed). The Episode Pass requirement on some quest rewards is a purchase requirement and is excluded (O33) (tier: directly observed). The hard mode five-per-day limit is a rate limiter and is excluded (O16) (tier: directly observed). The next campaign node is the next unit of the campaign and is excluded (O32) (tier: directly observed).
**Variants present:** Level gate (O30). Composite gate, for dark side battles, mod battles, ships and guild raids (O31). Stage gate, for hard mode, mod challenges and the Journey Guide route through Rebels 5 (O10, O31, O32). Count gate, for collecting one datacron and holding three dark side characters (O31). Opaque gate, for tables represented only by a requirement message (O30). Undescribed gate, for the Scavenger, where the narrator asks what relic amplifiers are (O31). Staggered gates (O30). Announced unlock gate, through level-up messages and guide introductions (O22). Silent unlock gate, for Allies (O30). Bypassable gate, for the Journey Guide's "player level 27 or complete Rebels 5" (O31).
**Variants not established:** Browsable gate, because whether locked features can be explored before unlocking was not shown. Previewed gate. Reinstating gate. Per-position gate.
**Alternative considered:** Leveling and Milestone classify the measure and the crossing and are tagged separately. Seasonal Progression Pass was considered for the pass-only quest rewards, which the purchase exclusion removes from this tag. Energy was considered for the hard mode daily limit, which governs how often rather than whether.

tags.name: Energy
tags.confidence:
directly observed
**Role:** engagement, monetization
Energy limits how many battles and simulations run in a session (O15, O17), and refills and energy grants are sold for crystals and inside paid bundles (O15, O58).
**Rationale:** Galaxy of Heroes maintains bounded energy pools with a stated maximum that rises with player level (O15) (tier: directly observed). Starting a light side battle consumes 6 energy and a cantina battle 8 cantina energy (O15) (tier: directly observed). Remaining energy limited how many simulations the narrator could run despite holding enough sim tickets (O17) (tier: directly observed). Cantina energy regenerates one point every 12 minutes and can be refilled for crystals, and level-ups grant bonus energy (O15) (tier: directly observed). The hard mode limit of five completions per day fits a scheduled-refill attempt allowance, but only the guide's statement was recorded and whether the limit blocks play or only rewards was not seen (O16) (tier: plausible).
**Variants present:** Per-action energy (O15). Action-specific energy, with separate energy, cantina energy and ship energy pools (O15). Variable-cost energy, at 6 and 8 per battle (O15). Time-regenerating energy, for cantina energy (O15). Purchasable-refill energy, at 100 crystals for 120 cantina energy (O15). Earned-refill energy, with 20 bonus energy per level-up (O15, O22).
**Variants not established:** Soft-depletion energy against a full block, because energy never ran out on the recording. The regeneration rate of standard energy. Scheduled-refill energy for the hard mode limit, held at plausible. Overdraft energy, because energy above the maximum was a surplus rather than a negative balance.
**Alternative considered:** Lives was considered and does not apply, because energy is consumed by starting battles rather than removed on failure. Spendable Credits and Tokens was considered and does not apply to energy, because the player makes no exchange choice when a battle deducts it. Evidence that would settle the hard mode question is a session showing a sixth hard completion attempted on one day.

observations.name: Episode Track

observations.name: Player-level gates
observations.observed: Almost every hub table is padlocked at first, with tapping one stating the requirement, often through the character standing at it. Stated player level requirements include the newsletter, achievements, daily quests, shipments, cantina battles, challenges, squads, allies, chat, events, the Coliseum, guilds, guild activities, ships and fleets collection tabs, the arena table, galactic tables, galactic war, championships and conquest. Allies opened at level 18 without any prompt, the navigation button simply became usable.

observations.name: Bronzium data card
observations.observed: The first item in the store's Featured tab is the Bronzium Data Card, marked free, offering ten free draws a day of an item or character, drawn from more than 200 possible items and 33 possible characters. After a free draw a countdown shows the next free draw in about 9 to 10 minutes, and free draws produced different results each time, shards, crafting items, a character unlock and gear. The draw animation can be skipped.

observations.name: Shipment tabs
observations.observed: At level 7, shipments unlock, with Featured Shipments refreshing every few hours and episode shipments refreshing weekly. Tabs listed include Cantina Battles, Guild Activity, Squad Arena, Galactic War, Mods, Fleet Arena, Guilds, Guild Events, Grand Arena, Shard Shop and Conquest, most locked at first, with an Episode Shipments tab appearing later. Featured items include character shards and upgrade items priced in crystals or credits, and the selection can be refreshed for 50 credits.

observations.name: Inbox grants and notices
observations.observed: The inbox unlocks after the first login reward claim. A welcome message grants 200 crystals, and claiming it removes the message. Further messages state that a character's shards are now farmable from a specific battle type, and that another character has been added to a list of accelerated characters, increasing its shard supply and shard shop conversion rate, with a link to a forum post on the shard economy. Messages can be deleted or kept.

tags.name: Progression Gate

directly observed
**Role:** engagement

Each withheld part is distinct from the measure it reads (tier: directly observed). Bypassable gate, for the Journey Guide's "player level 27 or complete Rebels 5" (O31).

observations.name: EA Connect linking
observations.observed: Beneath the inbox tabs, an EA Connect button offers a seamless cross-platform experience and a reward for connecting, pointing at credits shown as zero. Tapping it opens EA account sign-in with account creation, sign-in by email or phone, and options to stay signed in or sign in as invisible. The reward for connecting was not received, and its amount was not stated beyond the zero figure shown.

observations.name: Forum links
observations.observed: A Go button on an inbox message about accelerated characters opens the web browser at the game's forums, as does the inbox Forums tab, unlike EA Connect which opens inside the app. The forum shows recent posts and thread counts in the tens of thousands.

observations.name: Email ally invitation
observations.observed: The Allies Invite tab offers an invite by email, opening a pre-written email inviting the recipient to play the game with the sender. No reward to the inviter or the invitee is shown, and no prompt or reminder to invite was seen.

observations.name: Starter deal pop-ups
observations.observed: Immediately after naming, a pop-up offers an Ultimate First Order Starter Deal with no price or contents shown, only a Go button. The offer page shows a full five-character squad unlocked at four stars, 500 crystals, credits, training droids, gear and materials, for $1.99, with no close button other than a route back to the store. Each later return to the hub brings another starter deal for a different faction.

tags.name: Energy
tags.confidence:
directly observed
**Role:** engagement, monetization
Energy limits how many battles and simulations run in a session (O15, O17), and refills and energy grants are sold for crystals and inside paid bundles (O15, O58).
**Rationale:** Galaxy of Heroes maintains bounded energy pools with a stated maximum that rises with player level (O15) (tier: directly observed). Starting a light side battle consumes 6 energy and a cantina battle 8 cantina energy (O15) (tier: directly observed). Remaining energy limited how many simulations the narrator could run despite holding enough sim tickets (O17) (tier: directly observed). Cantina energy regenerates one point every 12 minutes and can be refilled for crystals, and level-ups grant bonus energy (O15) (tier: directly observed). The hard mode limit of five completions per day fits a scheduled-refill attempt allowance, but only the guide's statement was recorded and whether the limit blocks play or only rewards was not seen (O16) (tier: plausible).
**Variants present:** Per-action energy (O15). Action-specific energy, with separate energy, cantina energy and ship energy pools (O15). Variable-cost energy, at 6 and 8 per battle (O15). Time-regenerating energy, for cantina energy (O15). Purchasable-refill energy, at 100 crystals for 120 cantina energy (O15). Earned-refill energy, with 20 bonus energy per level-up (O15, O22).
**Variants not established:** Soft-depletion energy against a full block, because energy never ran out on the recording. The regeneration rate of standard energy. Scheduled-refill energy for the hard mode limit, held at plausible. Overdraft energy, because energy above the maximum was a surplus rather than a negative balance.
**Alternative considered:** Lives was considered and does not apply, because energy is consumed by starting battles rather than removed on failure. Spendable Credits and Tokens was considered and does not apply to energy, because the player makes no exchange choice when a battle deducts it. Evidence that would settle the hard mode question is a session showing a sixth hard completion attempted on one day.

A further find-more-calendars control lists a $4.99 calendar with 30 days of rewards and a separate calendar with its own reward set and a shorter purchase window.

tags.name: Daily Claim Pack
tags.confidence:
strongly supported
**Role:** retention, monetization
Each calendar spreads its rewards across 30 days (O60), and two of the three calendars are sold (O60).
**Rationale:** The Jump to 85 Hyper Calendar is a single claim, limited to one, that the product describes as a "30 day calendar containing training droids and character shards" whose rewards "persist until all are claimed or calendar is replaced" (O60) (tier: directly observed). The Ultimate Starter Calendar sells 30 days of rewards for $4.99, and a Phoenix Squad Calendar has its own reward set (O60) (tier: directly observed). That each calendar releases one reward per day is read from the 30-day calendar framing rather than seen operating (tier: strongly supported).
**Variants present:** Month-length pack (O60). Purchasable pack (O60). Accumulating-claim pack, from the copy that rewards persist until claimed (O60).
**Variants not established:** Daily reward pack against another interval, held at strongly supported. Claim-based against automatic-grant. Non-stackable pack, suggested by "or calendar is replaced" but not seen. Upfront-and-recurring pack.
**Alternative considered:** Daily Login Rewards was considered and applies separately to the April calendar, which needs no activation (O64). Progression Fund was considered because the free calendar's name refers to level 85; its copy describes a 30-day calendar, so time rather than level releases the rewards. A session showing the second day's calendar reward would settle the interval.

observations.name: Episode Pass tiers
observations.observed: Activating the Episode Pass offers two tiers. The standard pass is $19.99, unlocking premium rewards on the Episode Track and exclusive episode quests. The higher tier immediately grants 50,000 episode points, advances 10 milestones on the track and unlocks 24 rewards instantly, priced at $49.99.

tags.name: Seasonal Progression Pass
tags.confidence:
directly observed
**Role:** engagement, monetization
Episode points from episode and character quests drive what the player does within sessions (O19, O26), and the pass lane, the higher tier with 50,000 episode points and the pass-only quest rewards are sold (O33, O61).
**Rationale:** The Episode Track belongs to a named episode of the Andor era and states that repeatable bonus rewards continue "until the Episode ends" (O26) (tier: directly observed). It holds 50 ordered rewards advanced by episode points from quests (O19, O26) (tier: directly observed). The narrator claims free-lane rewards that have been reached (O26) (tier: directly observed). A pass lane with larger rewards sits beside the free lane (O26, O61) (tier: directly observed).
**Variants present:** Dual-track pass (O26). Quest-driven pass (O19). Mixed-source pass, since the higher tier adds 50,000 episode points by purchase (O61). Repeatable-end pass (O26).
**Variants not established:** Retroactive-upgrade pass, resetting pass, post-season claim pass and time-gated pass. Recurring seasonal pass, suggested by the "Episode 2" name but not shown (tier: plausible).
**Alternative considered:** Progression Fund was considered and is excluded, because the track states an end. Season Content Pass was considered and does not apply, because the pass opens a reward lane and quests rather than a bundle of content releases.

observations.name: Character sources and bundles
observations.observed: The Find control on a character lists where it can be obtained, including quest rewards, specific battle nodes, and a list of bundles and packs. For one character, the list includes a $49.99 bundle, multiple crystal-priced mega packs and data packs, and the Hyperdrive Bundle and Chromium packs.

tags.name: Set Collection
tags.confidence:
directly observed
**Role:** engagement, monetization
The roster shows which characters are held and which are missing, with shard counts toward each (O28), and Find routes a missing character to bundles and packs (O62).
**Rationale:** The Characters tab maintains member-level state for a defined set, shown through activated and not-activated filters, the guide's reference to "all the characters you have yet to unlock", and shard progress such as 2 of 25 on locked characters (O28) (tier: directly observed). Acquiring shards for Count Dooku does not unlock him, while Darth Vader activates at 25 shards (O28) (tier: directly observed). The Era of Andor view lists seven collectible era units (O29) (tier: directly observed). Whether that view tracks which era units are held was not described (tier: directly observed).
**Variants present:** Quantity-per-member collection, with shard counts per character (O28, O38).
**Variants not established:** Multi-set collection for era units, open-catalog collection, completion-tier collection and duplicate-bearing collection. No overall completion count was recorded.
**Alternative considered:** Companion was considered for the same characters and is not applied, for the reason given under Entries considered and not applied. An inventory reading without set tracking is ruled out by the not-activated filter and the shard counts on characters not yet held.

observations.name: April login rewards
observations.observed: On a second launch, a pop-up shows a monthly login calendar expiring within the month, stating that rewards reset at midnight, cannot be reclaimed if missed, and that daily login progress resets at the start of each month. The calendar runs from day 1 to day 30 for this player regardless of the calendar date, and a later day's claim button states how many more logins are needed. Rewards include credits rising across the month, an ability material, crystals, shards, training droids and special materials. Collecting the day 1 reward is followed by the inbox unlocking.

tags.name: Daily Login Rewards
tags.confidence:
directly observed
**Role:** retention
The April calendar's stated rule, that rewards reset daily and missed rewards cannot be reclaimed, ties each reward to returning within a day (O64).
**Rationale:** The pop-up defines daily windows resetting at midnight and tells the player to log in daily to collect (O64) (tier: directly observed). The narrator claims the day 1 reward, and a later reward reads "Login 28 times to claim" (O64) (tier: directly observed). Access alone qualifies according to the stated rule (tier: directly observed). The inbox carries a Daily Login Rewards tab (O43) (tier: directly observed).
**Variants present:** Sequential daily reward, advancing by count of login days (O64). Expiring daily reward, since missed rewards cannot be reclaimed (O64).
**Variants not established:** Consecutive daily reward, because no continuity effect was stated. Claims beyond day 1 were not recorded. Tiered daily reward.
**Alternative considered:** Streak was considered and does not apply, because missed days do not reset or alter the sequence under the stated rule. Daily Claim Pack does not apply, because no prior activation governs these rewards.

Credits, cantina tokens and sim tickets are earned by playing and spent on upgrades, shipments and instant completions within sessions (O17, O35, O37), and ally points are earned only by fielding another player's unit (O36, O45).

Crystals also have stated non-paid earning paths (O34) (tier: directly observed).
**Variants present:** Activity-earned soft currency (O35, O37). Quest-earned soft currency, through the daily prize box (O18). Login-grant soft currency, through login reward credits (O64). Social-earned soft currency, for ally points (O36). General-purpose soft currency, for credits (O35). Restricted soft currency, for cantina tokens and ally points (O36, O37). Dual-path soft currency, for crystals and credits (O34, O35). Multi-currency soft-currency system (O34 to O37).

observations.observed: On the second launch, the system asks whether the app may send notifications. Later, an in-app pop-up asks the player to turn notifications on to receive updates about events in the galaxy, with a Remind Me Later option beside it. Tapping to turn notifications on at this point returns to the battles screen, since notifications are already on.

The store badge marks a free Bronzium draw or free gift packs, the Quests badge marks claimable quests, and a Collection badge marks gear ready to equip without the app explaining what it means when it first appears. A character with enough shards shows a red dot and a green Activate label.

observations.name: Countdowns and events board
observations.observed: From the first hub view, timers show a countdown for the Coliseum and for an upcoming character event. Offers carry their own countdowns throughout. The events board, once opened, lists solo events, some gated behind levels, challenges, guild raids and guild events, with an event shown active for weeks ahead.

observations.name: Era launch announcements
observations.observed: After the second battle of first launch, a pop-up announces a new era with a new character journey, a new marquee, a new roster of era units and new bosses. A later return, after an unrecorded gap in play, announces a further new era tied to a film release, again with a new marquee, roster and bosses.

observations.name: Film tie-in update
observations.observed: Before a later return, the app icon changes to artwork for an upcoming film, and a client update is required before opening. A new loading screen shows characters from the film, and the cantina guide greets the returning player with dialogue referencing the app's redesigned look and a removed character.

observations.name: Free character offer
observations.observed: Leaving the events board on a later return brings a free offer expiring in a stated number of days, granting shards for four characters, training droids and credits, framed with the same purchase-limit language as paid offers despite costing nothing. Claiming it delivers the items through the inbox, followed by an Activate Character prompt for the featured character, who can then be equipped and levelled immediately.

observations.name: Newsletter pop-up
observations.observed: Trying to return to the home screen around level 10 brings up a newsletter pop-up about the current era. Its Go button, expected to lead to the inbox, instead opens an offer pop-up with its own countdown.

systemView: Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes is a complex system whose spine is the character roster: every currency, quest, energy pool and gate ties back to acquiring, leveling or fielding one of the roster's more than 300 characters, and the game shows every locked one alongside the ones already held.

mechanicWriteups.name: Leveling
mechanicWriteups.summary: Player level and four separate character tracks, level, star rank, gear tier and ability, all advance independently.
mechanicWriteups.observed: Player level rises from battles and quest claims, reaching 16 by the end of play. Each character separately advances a character level raised with training droids, a star rank from one to seven raised by promotion, a gear tier raised by filling six equipment slots, and ability levels from one to eight raised with ability materials. The Era of Andor view also shows a total era level with a reward at the next level.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Player level sits at the top of the hub with a numeric count. Each character's four tracks appear on that character's own screen, with a training droid slot, a promotion prompt once enough shards are held, a gear-equip screen, and ability upgrade tiles.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Galaxy of Heroes runs five separate leveling tracks at once, one for the account and four per character, each spent from its own resource, training droids, shards, gear pieces and ability materials, and each capped differently, seven stars, eight ability levels. The era level sits apart from all of them with no stated rule for what advances it.
findings: Player level and four character tracks (level, star rank, gear tier, ability level) advance separately.
Character level is raised with training droids, star rank by promotion with shards and credits.
Gear tier rises once six equipment slots are filled; ability levels rise with ability materials.
An era level exists with a reward named at the next level, with no stated advancement rule.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: a character's four upgrade tracks in one view, and the era level screen showing its next reward.

mechanicWriteups.name: Experience Points
mechanicWriteups.summary: Battles, quest claims and character training each pay a separate XP value toward player level or character level.
mechanicWriteups.observed: The rewards screen states that battles earn player XP, a daily quest lists an XP reward, and claiming journey quests grants XP. Player XP accumulates toward player level, shown at 6 of 10 at level 2. Character training fills a separate character XP bar, such as 0 of 25, with higher-grade training droids granting more XP per use.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Player XP is not shown as its own balance; it surfaces only through the level progress indicator. Character XP appears as its own bar on a character's training screen.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Two separate XP values run side by side, one for the account and one per character, fed by different activities, battles and quest claims for the first, training droids for the second, and neither is shown as an exchangeable balance in its own right.
findings: Battles, quest claims and journey quest completion each grant player XP.
Player XP is shown only through the level progress indicator, not as its own figure.
Character training fills a separate character XP bar, shown as a fraction.
Higher-grade training droids grant more character XP per use.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: the player level progress bar, and a character's XP bar during training.

mechanicWriteups.name: Milestone
mechanicWriteups.summary: Level-up screens name exactly what has just unlocked and what unlocks next, beyond the number changing.
mechanicWriteups.observed: A player level-up produces its own screen stating what has just opened, such as shipments or challenges, and what opens at a future level, alongside 20 bonus energy. Completing every normal battle in the first campaign stage produces a separate message unlocking hard mode for that stage.
mechanicWriteups.presented: The level-up screen appears immediately on crossing a level, naming the unlock and the next one to come, separately from the level number itself changing on the hub display.
mechanicWriteups.noting: The level-up screen does more than report a new number: it names the specific feature that just became available and previews the next one by level, turning an otherwise generic number change into two pieces of forward-looking information at once.
findings: Level-up screens name what has just unlocked, separate from the level number.
Level-up screens also preview what unlocks at a future level.
Every level-up grants 20 bonus energy.
Completing every normal battle in a stage separately unlocks hard mode with its own message.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: a level-up screen naming an unlock, and the hard mode unlock message.

mechanicWriteups.name: Progression Gate
mechanicWriteups.summary: Nearly every hub table, mode and store tab stays locked behind a stated player level or character measure.
mechanicWriteups.observed: Almost every table in the hub is padlocked at first, with the requirement shown on tap: stated player levels for features including the newsletter, achievements, daily quests, shipments, cantina battles, challenges, squads, allies, events, guilds and championships. Other features combine a level with a roster or completion measure: dark side battles require three dark side characters, mod battles require a character trained to level 50, the shard store requires a character promoted to seven stars, and relic amplifiers require gear tier 13.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Locked tables sit in their eventual hub position from the very first screen, each stating its own requirement when tapped, so the whole feature map is visible before any of it opens.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Every locked feature the game shows a requirement for is gated on a measure the game itself advances through play, a level, a star rank, a gear tier, rather than on eligibility conditions such as purchases or guild membership; where a requirement also includes guild membership, only the level or gear portion of it is a gate of this kind.
findings: Nearly every hub table is visible but locked from the first screen.
Requirements shown include player level, dark side character count, character level, star rank and gear tier.
Locked features show exactly where they'll sit once unlocked.
Guild-membership requirements are separate from the level and gear conditions that gate access.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: the first hub view with its padlocked tables, and a locked table's requirement message.

mechanicWriteups.name: Energy
mechanicWriteups.summary: Three separate energy pools, regular, cantina and ship, each gate their own battle type and refill differently.
mechanicWriteups.observed: Starting a Light Side battle costs 6 energy and a cantina battle costs 8 cantina energy, with a separate ship energy pool for fleet battles. Cantina energy regenerates at one point every 12 minutes or can be refilled for crystals, and every player level-up raises the maximum and grants 20 bonus energy. Energy readings repeatedly exceeded the stated maximum throughout.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Each pool shows a current amount against a maximum near the relevant battle type, with a crystal-priced refill option offered directly where cantina energy is spent.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Frequent level-ups in the opening hours raised the energy maximum and granted bonus energy faster than battles spent it, so energy was never seen limiting play; readings sat well above the stated maximum throughout.
findings: Three separate energy pools gate light side battles, cantina battles and fleet battles.
A light side battle costs 6 energy; a cantina battle costs 8 cantina energy.
Cantina energy regenerates one point every 12 minutes or refills for crystals.
Every level-up raises the energy maximum and grants 20 bonus energy.
Energy readings exceeded the stated maximum throughout.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: the three energy pools on their respective battle screens, and a level-up screen stating the bonus energy granted.

mechanicWriteups.name: Daily / Weekly Quests
mechanicWriteups.summary: Four separate quest lists, daily, journey, episode and character, run alongside each other with their own reset rules.
mechanicWriteups.observed: Daily quests list seven objectives with a countdown to reset and progress tracked toward each, such as 18 of 100 energy used. Completing the full daily set opens a Daily Activity Prize Box. A new episode quest is added once a day, and character quests ask the player to win battles with or promote a featured character.
mechanicWriteups.presented: All four quest types share one Quests screen, split into tabs, each unlocking at a different point in early progression.
mechanicWriteups.noting: The daily quest list directs spending as much as activity, asking the player to open a data card in the store or buy shipments, so completing the list also completes a purchase-adjacent action inside the game's own economy.
findings: Daily quests list seven objectives with a countdown to reset.
Completing the daily set opens a Daily Activity Prize Box.
One new episode quest is added each day.
Character quests ask the player to win battles with or promote a featured character.
Some daily quests require spending in the store or shipments, not just battling.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: the daily quest list with its reset countdown, and the Daily Activity Prize Box message.

mechanicWriteups.name: Daily Login Rewards
mechanicWriteups.summary: A monthly calendar pays a growing reward for each day logged in, with missed days lost for good.
mechanicWriteups.observed: The April login calendar runs from day 1 to day 30, resetting at the start of each month, and states that rewards reset at midnight, cannot be reclaimed if missed, and count days logged in rather than calendar dates. Rewards grow from 20,000 credits on day 1 to 150,000 on day 28, with an ability material, crystals, shards, training droids and materials at other days.
mechanicWriteups.presented: The calendar appears as a pop-up on returning to the app, stating the days remaining in the current month and greying out days not yet reachable, with a label stating how many more logins are needed for the next unclaimed reward.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Because the calendar counts logins rather than calendar days and starts fresh each month regardless of when in the month a player begins, a player who starts partway through a month cannot reach every day's reward even by logging in daily for the rest of it.
findings: The calendar runs day 1 to day 30, resetting at the start of each month.
Rewards reset at midnight and cannot be reclaimed once missed.
The calendar counts days logged in, not calendar dates.
Credits rise from 20,000 on day 1 to 150,000 on day 28.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: the login calendar pop-up, and a greyed-out day stating how many more logins are needed.

mechanicWriteups.name: Daily Claim Pack
mechanicWriteups.summary: A free 30-day calendar and two purchasable ones each release their own reward set day by day.
mechanicWriteups.observed: A free calendar named for level 85 describes itself as containing training droids and character shards across 30 days, with rewards stated to persist until all are claimed or the calendar is replaced. A purchasable calendar sells 30 days of rewards for $4.99, and a further purchasable calendar carries its own separate reward set.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Calendars are offered from the store rather than a login pop-up, each named and priced on its own listing, distinct from the April login rewards calendar shown elsewhere.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Despite one calendar's name referencing a target level, its own description frames the release as running across 30 days rather than by level reached, and a player could hold this calendar, a purchased one and the separate April login calendar all at once, each releasing on its own schedule.
findings: A free calendar spans 30 days of training droids and character shards.
Its rewards persist until claimed or the calendar is replaced.
A purchasable calendar sells 30 days of rewards for $4.99.
A further purchasable calendar carries its own separate reward set.
These calendars run alongside, and separately from, the April login rewards calendar.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: the free calendar's description screen, and the purchasable calendar's store listing.

mechanicWriteups.name: Seasonal Progression Pass
mechanicWriteups.summary: An Episode Track pays free and paid reward lanes from quest-earned points, with a purchase that fills lanes instantly.
mechanicWriteups.observed: At level 10 the Episode Track opens for a named episode, tracking points earned from episode and character quests toward 50 ordered rewards on a free lane, with a paid lane beside it showing visibly larger rewards. The track states that repeatable bonus rewards continue until the episode ends. Buying the Episode Pass unlocks the paid lane and pass-only quest rewards; a higher tier immediately grants 50,000 episode points, advances 10 milestones and unlocks 24 rewards at once.
mechanicWriteups.presented: The Episode Track sits as a featured entry beside Quests once unlocked, with the free and paid lanes shown side by side and unclaimed rewards visibly waiting further along the track.
mechanicWriteups.noting: The higher purchase tier doesn't just unlock the paid lane, it also advances the track itself by a stated amount instantly, so the same purchase both opens a benefit and skips a portion of the progress needed to reach further rewards inside it.
findings: The Episode Track holds a free lane and a larger paid lane, fed by episode and character quest points.
The track states that its bonus rewards run until the episode ends.
The Episode Pass unlocks the paid lane and pass-only quest rewards.
A higher pass tier immediately grants 50,000 episode points and unlocks 24 rewards at once.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: the Episode Track showing both lanes, and the higher pass tier's instant-grant offer.

mechanicWriteups.name: Achievement
mechanicWriteups.summary: An Achievements tab claims individual rewards for criteria the game already tracked before the tab was even opened.
mechanicWriteups.observed: On unlocking the Achievements tab, five achievements are already complete from earlier play, each claimed individually for its own reward of gear, credits or other items. The full list of achievements can be browsed beyond the completed ones.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Achievements sit in their own tab, reached once player level opens it, with completed and uncompleted criteria browsable in one list and a claim action on each completed entry.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Achievements were already satisfied by ordinary play before the tab itself unlocked, so the first thing the tab shows a player is a backlog of rewards waiting on progress that happened before the feature existed for them.
findings: Five achievements are already complete when the Achievements tab first opens.
Each achievement is claimed individually for its own reward.
The full achievement list, completed and uncompleted, can be browsed.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: the Achievements tab on first opening, showing already-completed entries.

mechanicWriteups.name: Challenge
mechanicWriteups.summary: A Challenges table runs tiered battles against changed rules, open only on specific days of the week.
mechanicWriteups.observed: The Challenges table opens named challenges such as a Training Droids challenge, a Bounty Hunter challenge and an Ability Materials challenge, each open only on stated days of the week. Each challenge has six tiers, with details, possible rewards and required-unit tabs, and the first tier of the Training Droids challenge is completed through three battles against a boss that heals to full health regularly.
mechanicWriteups.presented: The table opens with an introduction naming what challenges test, and each challenge lists its own open days, tier structure and requirements before a battle starts.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Framing a challenge tier around a specific boss behavior, a boss that heals regularly, asks the player to bring a specific answer, a way to block healing, rather than simply a stronger squad, which is a different kind of test than the ordinary campaign battles.
findings: Challenges are named and open only on specific days of the week.
Each challenge has six tiers with details, rewards and required-unit information.
The first tier of one challenge is completed through three battles.
One challenge's boss heals to full health regularly, calling for a specific counter.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: the Challenges table with its named challenges and open days, and one challenge's tier list.

mechanicWriteups.name: Set Collection
mechanicWriteups.summary: A roster of more than 300 characters tracks shard progress toward every character, held or not yet unlocked.
mechanicWriteups.observed: The Characters tab shows both the characters the player has and, in the game's own words, all the characters still to unlock, with more than 300 in total. Locked characters show shard progress toward the amount needed to activate them, and a character with enough shards shows a badge inviting activation. Filters include allegiance, faction, role and whether a character is activated, with sorting by gear tier, health, speed, potency and power.
mechanicWriteups.presented: The full roster is visible in one tab regardless of whether each character is held, with locked entries showing a shard count and unlocked entries showing full stats and filters.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Showing every character the game has, not just the ones already held, turns the roster into a visible target list rather than a private inventory, and shard progress on locked characters gives every one of them, met or not, a stated distance still to go.
findings: More than 300 characters are shown, including ones not yet unlocked.
Locked characters display shard progress toward the amount needed to activate them.
Filters include allegiance, faction, role and activation status; sorting includes gear tier and power.
A character with enough shards shows a badge inviting activation.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: the Characters tab showing both held and locked characters, and a locked character's shard progress.

mechanicWriteups.name: Loot Box
mechanicWriteups.summary: Crystal-priced Chromium packs and an ally-point Bronzium draw each resolve to characters or shards from a stated pool.
mechanicWriteups.observed: A Chromium Mega Pack costs 2,520 crystals and resolves eight cards drawn from 120 possible characters and 120 possible shard sets, with one card guaranteed to award a character and each card's odds stated at 20% for a character against 80% for a shard set. A single Chromium Data Card costs 350 crystals with no guarantee, and an extra Bronzium data card draw, beyond the free daily allowance, costs 250 ally points and resolves to an item or character from a stated pool.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Each pack's full possible-outcome pool, every character and every shard set it can produce, can be viewed in detail before a purchase is made.
mechanicWriteups.noting: The odds and the full outcome pool are stated up front for every paid pack, down to the percentage split between a character and a shard set on each card, so nothing about what a purchase can produce is withheld from view before it's bought.
findings: A Chromium Mega Pack costs 2,520 crystals for eight cards with one guaranteed character.
Each card is stated at 20% character odds against 80% shard set odds.
A single Chromium Data Card costs 350 crystals with no guarantee.
An extra Bronzium draw beyond the free daily allowance costs 250 ally points.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: the Chromium Mega Pack's stated odds screen, and the extra Bronzium draw's ally-point price.

mechanicWriteups.name: Variable Reward Outcome
mechanicWriteups.summary: A free daily Bronzium draw and a shared prize box each resolve to different rewards without any price paid.
mechanicWriteups.observed: A free Bronzium data card draw is offered up to ten times a day with no cost, resolving to different results across multiple draws: character shards, crafting items, a character unlock and gear. The Daily Activity Prize Box, opened after completing the day's quests, states that the player receives one or more of a listed set of items.
mechanicWriteups.presented: The free draw sits on the same card as the paid draw, refreshing on a visible countdown of several minutes once used, with the animation skippable.
mechanicWriteups.noting: The free draw and the paid draw beside it look identical on screen, a card, a countdown, an open action, but only the paid one asks the player to commit anything before the result is known, which is what separates a variable outcome from a loot box on the very same surface.
findings: A free Bronzium draw is offered up to ten times a day at no cost.
Free draws resolved to shards, crafting items, a character unlock and gear across multiple draws.
The Daily Activity Prize Box states it grants one or more of a listed set of items.
The free draw sits on the same card as the paid, ally-point-priced draw.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: the free Bronzium draw with its refresh countdown, and the Daily Activity Prize Box message.

mechanicWriteups.name: Hard Currency
mechanicWriteups.summary: Crystals are sold in five money-priced packages and spent on packs, shipments, energy refills and credit conversion.
mechanicWriteups.observed: Crystals are sold for real money in five packages, from 610 for $4.99 up to 15,710 for $99.99, with more crystals per dollar in larger packages. The same balance buys Chromium packs, refreshes cantina energy, and converts into credits through crystal-priced credit packs. A welcome gift and login rewards also grant crystals without payment.
mechanicWriteups.presented: The Crystals tab in the store lists all five packages together, while crystal prices for other purchases, energy refills, packs, credit conversion, appear on their own respective screens.
mechanicWriteups.noting: The same crystal balance is reachable by paying or by ordinary play, a welcome gift and login rewards both grant it free, which means every crystal-priced purchase in the game can, in principle, be reached without spending money, just more slowly.
findings: Crystals sell in five packages from 610 for $4.99 to 15,710 for $99.99.
Larger packages give more crystals per dollar.
Crystals buy Chromium packs, energy refills and credit conversion packs.
A welcome gift and login rewards grant crystals without payment.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: the Crystals tab showing all five packages, and a crystal-priced item such as an energy refill.

mechanicWriteups.name: Soft Currency
mechanicWriteups.summary: Credits, cantina tokens and ally points are each earned through play and spent on their own upgrade paths.
mechanicWriteups.observed: Credits are earned from battles and spent on training, activation, promotion, ability upgrades and shipment purchases. Cantina battle tokens are earned per cantina battle win and spent in a dedicated cantina store. Ally points are earned only by fielding a borrowed unit in battle and are spendable on extra Bronzium draws and weekly shipment items.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Each currency is shown near where it's earned, credits on the battle rewards screen, cantina tokens after a cantina battle, ally points after a battle that used a borrowed unit, and each is spent on its own dedicated screens.
mechanicWriteups.noting: Ally points are the one currency here that can only be earned through another player's presence in the squad, by way of a borrowed unit, which ties this currency's entire supply to the borrowing system rather than to the player's own activity alone.
findings: Credits are earned from battles and spent on character upgrades and shipments.
Cantina battle tokens are earned per win and spent in the cantina store.
Ally points are earned only by fielding a borrowed unit in battle.
Ally points are spent on extra Bronzium draws and weekly shipment items.
mechanicWriteups.screenshotsNote: the credits balance on a battle rewards screen, and the ally points earned after a battle with a borrowed unit.

mechanicWriteups.name: Spendable Credits and Tokens
mechanicWriteups.summary: Lightspeed tokens are described as applying to any character to upgrade stars, abilities, gear or relic levels.
mechanicWriteups.observed: Lightspeed tokens are introduced as units that can be applied to individual characters to quickly upgrade their stars, abilities, gear tiers and relic amplifier levels, described as one of the fastest ways to upgrade a roster. None were held or available to apply at first, and a later search shows them offered as a reward on the Episode Track.
mechanicWriteups.presented: Tokens have their own screen inside a character's inventory, listing which are held and which are available elsewhere, with an apply action for any token on hand.
mechanicWriteups.noting: The token's own description names four separate things it can upgrade at once, stars, abilities, gear and relic levels, which makes it a single unit that can substitute for several of the game's other upgrade currencies depending on where the player chooses to apply it.
findings: Lightspeed tokens apply to a character to upgrade stars, abilities, gear tiers or relic levels.
No tokens were held or available to apply at the point they were introduced.
The Episode Track is the only source shown for lightspeed tokens.
Tokens have a dedicated screen inside each character's own inventory.

the lightspeed token screen inside a character's inventory, and the Episode Track reward offering one.

sectionCards.access: Player-level gates on nearly every hub table, combined gates on specific features, and gates inside already-open activities make up this section.
sectionCards.economy: Crystals, credits, ally points, cantina tokens, shards and lightspeed tokens run alongside the store's Bronzium card and shipment tabs.
sectionCards.social: Allies, borrowed units, ally requests and player profiles run alongside guild and arena surfaces that stay locked throughout.
sectionCards.reach: EA Connect linking, forum links and an email invitation to become allies are the app's routes outside itself.
sectionCards.monetization: Starter deal pop-ups, a five-tab store, crystal and Chromium packs, and an Episode Pass make up this section.
sectionCards.returns: Login rewards, a notification pre-prompt, red badge counters and countdown timers on offers and events bring the player back.

proposedTags.name: Borrowed Unit
proposedTags.draftDefinition: A borrowed unit is a persistent entity held by another identified user that the product offers to the current user for a single activity instance, placed in a position reserved for such units alongside the user's own entities, whose use pays the borrower a stated reward, and after which the product may prompt the borrower to form a standing relationship with the lender.
proposedTags.conditions: A roster of persistent acting entities held by many users, so that other users' entities are available to offer (O28, O45). A reserved position that does not displace the user's own entities (O45). A reward paid in a currency with its own sink (O36, O41). A relationship system into which the borrower can be invited after use (O44, O46).
proposedTags.whyNotCovered: Companion excludes entities that are another person's representation. Gifting requires a sender to initiate a grant, and the lender here takes no observed action. Referral requires an introduction followed by a completion event. Group Membership and Clan / Guild concern groups rather than a one-instance loan. Soft Currency covers the ally points earned but not the lending surface that produces them.
proposedTags.recurrenceElsewhere: Observed in this app only. No other app's sessions were consulted in this run, so recurrence is expected rather than observed.
proposedTags.caveat: The proposal remains open. It rests on one app, and the lender's side was never observed: whether lenders are rewarded or notified, how offered units are selected, and whether allies' units are offered differently from strangers' were all unseen. The recorded offers came from players inactive for thousands of days (O46), which may reflect this account's level band rather than the general rule. Either of two observations would settle it: a second app carrying the same shape, a unit held by another identified user placed in a reserved position for one activity instance with a stated reward to the borrower; or a session in this app showing what the lender receives when a unit is borrowed and whether the lender is notified.

proposedTags.name: Directed Objective List
proposedTags.draftDefinition: A directed objective list is a persistent, non-recurring set of product-defined objectives shown a few at a time, in which each objective carries a control that takes the user directly to the place where it is completed, and completing one releases the next.
proposedTags.conditions: A product with many surfaces and locked features, where the next useful action is not obvious (O4, O30). A guide or copy that establishes the list as the answer to what to do next (O5).
proposedTags.whyNotCovered: Daily / Weekly Quests requires a daily or weekly issuance or refresh rule, which journey quests do not show. Challenge requires an end boundary. Achievement records attained criteria after the fact. Milestone recognizes thresholds in a measure rather than issuing objectives.
proposedTags.recurrenceElsewhere: No other app's sessions were consulted in this run, so recurrence is expected rather than observed.
proposedTags.caveat: The proposal remains open. Its distinction from Daily / Weekly Quests holds, since nothing in the list is issued or refreshed on a period (O25). Whether the list ever runs out, expires or follows a fixed order was not observed, and that decides whether this is a mechanic or an onboarding checklist that ends once the first hours of guidance are over. A session showing the journey quest list at a later stage of play, either still issuing objectives or exhausted, would settle it. The same list surface also carries daily, episode and character quests, which are tagged on their own terms.

system.tagline: Every locked character shows exactly how to unlock it, and every gate, currency and quest ties back to the same roster of more than 300.
system.overview: Galaxy of Heroes shows its full 300-plus character roster from the start, locked and unlocked alike, with a Find control naming every acquisition path for a character still missing. Nearly every hub feature is visible but padlocked behind a stated player level or character measure. An Episode Track pays free and paid reward lanes from quest points, a wide currency system (crystals, credits, ally points, cantina tokens) funds both purchases and loot packs, and three separate energy pools gate light side, cantina and fleet battles.
system.loop: Battle to earn player XP, credits, shards, gear and energy-fed rewards. Player XP raises player level, which unlocks hub tables one at a time and raises the energy maximum. Character shards, credits, gear and ability materials raise a character's own level, star rank, gear tier and abilities, which in turn satisfy the roster-based conditions on higher-tier gates. Daily and episode quests direct spending and battling, paying episode points into the Episode Track, whose rewards include lightspeed tokens for upgrading characters. Crystals and ally points buy Chromium and Bronzium packs that resolve to more characters and shards, feeding the collection loop again.
system.keyInsight: Galaxy of Heroes routes nearly everything back to the same roster: XP raises the levels that open gates, quests pay the points and tokens that upgrade characters, and every currency, earned or bought, ends at a pack or a shipment that produces more characters or shards. The one mechanic that sits apart is the free daily draw, tagged separately from the paid packs it sits beside on the same card, since nothing is committed before it resolves.
system.whatMakesItWork: Because a character's level, star rank and gear tier are what most of the higher-tier gates actually check, upgrading the roster and clearing the gate map are the same activity seen from two angles, nothing about the gates asks the player to do anything the currency and quest systems weren't already pointing them toward. Showing the full 300-plus roster up front, locked entries included, turns that same activity into a visible, always-present list of specific next targets rather than an abstract grind.

roles.role: Player level and four separate per-character tracks, level, star rank, gear tier and ability, each advancing on its own resource.
Battles, quest claims and training each pay a separate XP value toward player level or a character's own level.
Level-up screens name exactly what has just unlocked and what unlocks next, beyond the level number itself.
Nearly every hub table, mode and store tab stays locked behind a stated player level or character measure.
Four parallel quest lists, daily, journey, episode and character, each unlocking at a different point and each with its own reset rule.
A monthly calendar pays a growing reward for each day logged in, with missed days lost for good.
A free 30-day calendar and two purchasable ones each release their own reward set day by day.
A Challenges table runs tiered battles against changed rules, open only on stated days of the week.
An Episode Track pays free and paid reward lanes from quest-earned points, with a purchase that fills lanes instantly.
An Achievements tab claims individual rewards for criteria the game already tracked before the tab was opened.
A roster of more than 300 characters tracks shard progress toward every character, held or not.
Crystal-priced Chromium packs and a paid Bronzium draw each resolve to characters or shards from a stated, viewable pool.
A free daily Bronzium draw and a shared prize box each resolve to different rewards with nothing committed up front.
Crystals sell in five money-priced packages and buy packs, shipments, energy refills and credit conversion.
Credits, cantina tokens and ally points are each earned through play and spent on their own upgrade paths.
Lightspeed tokens apply to any character to upgrade stars, abilities, gear or relic levels, sourced only from the Episode Track.
Three separate energy pools, regular, cantina and ship, gate their own battle type and refill on different rules.

connections.title: XP is what moves the level states
connections.desc: Battle, quest-claim and training XP accumulate toward player level and each character's own level, the values those tracks are stated against.
connections.effect: Nothing else has to change for a level to rise, the same activity that earns XP for any other reason is also progress toward it.

connections.title: The level-up screen is the milestone
connections.desc: The same level-up event that raises the player-level number also produces a separate screen naming what has just unlocked and what unlocks next.
connections.effect: A level crossing is never just a number changing, it's paired with a stated recognition of what that crossing specifically opened.

connections.title: Leveling funds the pool it will later spend
connections.desc: Every level-up raises the energy maximum and grants 20 bonus energy on top of it.
connections.effect: Frequent early level-ups keep energy running ahead of what battles spend it on, so the pool rarely constrains play in the opening hours.

connections.title: Levels are what most gates actually check
connections.desc: Player level, character level, star rank and gear tier, all Leveling's own tracks, are the specific measures nearly every locked hub table states as its requirement.
connections.effect: Upgrading a character for any other reason is very often also clearing the exact condition a locked feature is waiting on.

connections.title: The daily quest set pays into the currency economy
connections.desc: Completing the day's quest list opens a prize box of credits and other spendable materials.
connections.effect: A player working through daily quests for their own sake is also restocking the balances the rest of the economy draws on.

connections.title: Episode quests are the Episode Track's main input
connections.desc: Episode and character quests are named as the biggest source of the points that advance the Episode Track, with some quest rewards reserved for Episode Pass holders.
connections.effect: A quest list a free player already works through is also what a paying player is buying faster access to.

connections.title: The only stated source for lightspeed tokens
connections.desc: Lightspeed tokens, applicable to a character's stars, abilities, gear or relic levels, are found only as a reward on the Episode Track.
connections.effect: Reaching further into the Episode Track is the one shown way to reach this particular upgrade currency, whichever lane it sits on.

connections.title: Crystals are what Chromium packs cost
connections.desc: Every Chromium pack, from a single Data Card to the Mega Pack, is priced in crystals.
connections.effect: However crystals were obtained, paid or earned free, they convert directly into a chance at more characters and shards through the same paid-pack surface.

connections.title: Ally points buy the one paid Bronzium draw
connections.desc: An extra Bronzium draw beyond the free daily allowance costs 250 ally points, the same balance earned only by fielding a borrowed unit.
connections.effect: The borrowing system, not ordinary battling, is what funds this particular paid draw.

connections.title: Paid packs resolve into the roster
connections.desc: Chromium packs and the paid Bronzium draw both resolve to characters or character shard sets from a stated pool.
connections.effect: A purchase here has nowhere else to land but the same roster the free draw and ordinary play also feed.

connections.title: The free draw reaches the roster too
connections.desc: The free daily Bronzium draw resolved to character shards and a character unlock alongside crafting items and gear.
connections.effect: A player who never pays still has a route into the same roster the paid packs feed, just without anything committed up front.
